title: Some Raindrops Can Slowly Wear Away Metal
summary:
Raindrops may be hurting cars, bridges and statues more than people knew. But only some raindrops do it: the ones with an electric charge.

Drops can get a charge when they slide over leaves, glass or buildings. When these drops land on metal, they can pass the charge along. Over time, this makes the metal slowly wear away. This is called corrosion.

Scientist Zhongyuan Ni found this by accident. He left an experiment running while he went for coffee. When he came back, the copper looked different!

His team tested copper covered in Teflon, a strong coating. Charged drops wore through the coating and damaged the copper. Drops without a charge did no harm.

Ni says not to worry, because the effect is small. But after many years outside, it can add up. The discovery could help make better coatings.
why_it_matters: Bridges, cars and playgrounds you use every day could last longer if scientists make better coatings.
